description: Use when configuring OmniStudio at the org level: enabling Standard Runtime, selecting the Runtime Namespace, assigning Permission Set Licenses, toggling feature settings, and granting Experience Cloud community access. Trigger keywords: OmniStudio Settings, Standard OmniStudio Runtime, managed package runtime, runtime namespace, OmniStudio Permission Set, OmniStudio PSL. NOT for moving an org off the vlocity namespace — use omnistudio/vlocity-to-native-omnistudio-migration. NOT for deciding whether to adopt OmniStudio — use architect/omnistudio-vs-standard-decision.
inputs: org edition and OmniStudio license type (Industries or standalone OmniStudio)
target runtime mode: Standard OmniStudio Runtime (native) or Managed Package Runtime
installed managed-package namespace, read from Installed Packages, if migrating or running a legacy install
user populations requiring OmniStudio access: internal builders, internal consumers, Experience Cloud community members
name: omnistudio-admin-configuration
official_sources: Security Implementation Guide (Summer '26) — a permission set that needs a user or permission set license can be assigned only to users who hold it, which is why license assignment precedes permission set assignment: secguide 262 L1999-2004.

Salesforce DX Developer Guide (Winter '27) — OmniStudio licensing is split into runtime, designer and metadata features (`OmnistudioRuntime`, `OmnistudioDesigner`, `OmnistudioMetadata`) and add-on licenses such as `OmniStudioRuntimeCCAddon`: sfdx_dev 264 L8554-8571, L6929.
Metadata API Developer Guide (Winter '27) — "OmniStudio Admin" named as a permission set license: api_meta 264 L56731-56732.
Salesforce DX Developer Guide (Winter '27) — OmniStudio component metadata types `OmniDataTransform`, `OmniIntegrationProcedure`, `OmniScript`, `OmniUiCard`: sfdx_dev 264 L16493-16496.

UNVERIFIED (2026-10-21): the Salesforce Help topics below are outside the corpus and cannot be re-fetched (help.salesforce.com); the two marked "verified 2026-08-14" were read by an earlier pass. They are the only source for the OmniStudio Settings toggles, Runtime Namespace, `OmniStudioPSL` and Enhanced Runtime Performance claims.
Salesforce Help: OmniStudio Permission Sets and Licenses — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.os_permission_sets_and_licenses.htm
Salesforce Help: Standard OmniStudio Content and Runtime — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.os_standard_content_and_runtime.htm
Salesforce Help: Disable Managed Package Runtime — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.os_disable_managed_package_runtime.htm

Salesforce Help: Enable Enhanced Runtime Performance of Components — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.os_setting_runtime_perf.htm — source for the setting's Before You Begin items: that it makes all components execute in user mode, the Omni Interaction Access Configuration object prerequisite, the do-not-enable-directly-in-production warning, and that it gates `ConnectAPI.OmniDesignerConnect.integrationProcedureExecute` (when disabled, Integration Procedure calls from Apex do not route through the Connect API). The page states no release. (verified 2026-08-14)

Salesforce Help: Omnistudio Settings — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.os_omnistudio_settings.htm — corroborates the setting's presence on the Settings page and the phrasing quoted above: it "ensures that Omnistudio communicates with the Salesforce Platform with in-platform capabilities instead of through Apex calls," and "User mode respects the access levels of the person performing an operation." (verified 2026-08-14)
outputs: permission set assignment plan for admins, users, and community members
runtime mode verification steps and post-activation checks
